mainTopic: The נזיר-on-the-day-משיח-comes ברייתא and תחומין above ten טפחים; רבן גמליאל's measuring tube; נחמיה outside the תחום and the human partition.
overview: The גמרא is trying to answer whether תחומין (the שבת travel limits) apply in the air, more than ten טפחים above the ground. It uses a ברייתא about someone who vowed to be a נזיר on the day בן דוד comes: he may drink wine on שבת and יום טוב but not on weekdays. First it seems the ברייתא proves יש תחומין. Then the גמרא suggests a different reason: אליהו comes the day before משיח, and there is a promise that אליהו never comes on ערב שבת or ערב יום טוב. Next the גמרא asks why Sunday is not permitted, which seems to prove אין תחומין. It answers that the תנא was unsure about תחומין and ruled strictly, so the ברייתא proves nothing either way. The גמרא then explains that the permission applies only when the vow was made on שבת or יום טוב itself. Next it returns to the משנה about רבן גמליאל's boat. It explains that he had a tube for measuring 2,000 אמות, and adds some practical measuring tricks. Finally it tells of נחמיה, who walked past the תחום while learning, and רב נחמן's advice to make a human partition. It then begins asking what רב חסדא's exact doubt was, a discussion that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The vow-keeper may not drink wine on weekdays
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends by ruling that this נזיר may not drink wine on any weekday.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he is forbidden to drink wine on all the weekdays.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the last line of the ברייתא the גמרא just quoted. On שבת and יום טוב he may drink wine, but on every weekday he may not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On any weekday, משיח might already have arrived without this person knowing. If so, his נזירות has already started, so he must hold back from wine every weekday. The contrast between weekdays and שבת/יום טוב is what the גמרא is about to analyze.

keyTerms.meaning: To drink wine (the main thing a נזיר may not do)
Weekdays (days that are not שבת or יום טוב)

phrases.english: And he is forbidden to drink wine
phrases.notes: Refers to the person who vowed: 'I am a נזיר on the day בן דוד comes.'

phrases.english: all the weekdays.
phrases.notes: Because משיח might already have come today without his knowing.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָסוּר לִשְׁתּוֹת יַיִן כׇּל יְמוֹת הַחוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא quoted on the previous amud (permitted on שבת and יום טוב, forbidden on weekdays).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The נזיר-on-the-day-משיח-comes may not drink wine on any weekday.

steps.title: The ברייתא seems to prove that תחומין apply in the air
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא makes sense only if תחומין apply above ten טפחים. If they did not, why would wine be allowed on שבת?
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense if you say there are תחומין (above ten טפחים): that is why he may drink on שבת and יום טוב. But if you say there are no תחומין up there, why may he drink on שבת and יום טוב?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to use the ברייתא to answer its earlier question about תחומין in the air. It says the ברייתא only makes sense if תחומין apply even up high.
steps.deeperAnalysis: משיח might arrive miraculously, flying through the air from far away. If תחומין apply up high, he cannot travel to us on שבת, so on שבת our person is safe to drink. If תחומין do not apply up high, משיח could arrive on שבת too, and wine should be forbidden then as well.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense if you say… (opens an argument that one side fits)
Shabbat boundaries (the 2,000-אמה limit for walking outside a town)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with an ordinary question about נזירות. The real topic is תחומין למעלה מעשרה, whether Shabbat boundaries apply high in the air. The ברייתא about the נזיר is only being used as evidence.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the גמרא's first attempt to settle the open question of תחומין above ten טפחים, using a real ruling from a ברייתא.

phrases.english: It makes sense if you say there are Shabbat boundaries (above ten handbreadths) —
phrases.notes: First side of the question: boundaries apply even in the air.

phrases.english: that is why on Shabbat and Festivals he is permitted.
phrases.notes: משיח cannot travel to us on these days, even by air.

phrases.english: But if you say there are no boundaries (up there),
phrases.notes: Second side of the question.

phrases.english: why is he permitted on Shabbat and Festivals?
phrases.notes: משיח could fly in on שבת, so wine should be forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי אָמְרַתְּ בִּשְׁלָמָא יֵשׁ תְּחוּמִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the ruling of the ברייתא (including Step 1) as evidence for the question of תחומין in the air.
steps.raayaObject: That תחומין apply higher than ten טפחים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא permitting the vow-keeper to drink wine on שבת and יום טוב.

steps.title: A different reason: אליהו must come the day before
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes the proof away. Wine may be allowed on שבת for another reason: אליהו must come the day before משיח, and he did not come yesterday.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is different there, because the verse says: 'Behold, I am sending you אליהו הנביא…' And אליהו did not come yesterday.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers another reason the ברייתא allows wine on שבת, one that has nothing to do with תחומין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in מלאכי teaches that אליהו comes before משיח, understood as one day earlier. Since אליהו did not come yesterday, משיח cannot come today. This would explain the ברייתא's leniency on שבת even if there are no תחומין in the air, so the proof falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different there (a reason the case cannot be used as proof)
אליהו the prophet, who announces משיח

phrases.english: It is different there, because the verse says:
phrases.notes: Introduces a different reason for the ברייתא's ruling.

phrases.english: "Behold, I am sending to you
phrases.notes: מלאכי ג:כג

phrases.english: Elijah the prophet, etc.",
phrases.notes: The verse continues: 'before the coming of the great day of ה'.'

phrases.english: and Elijah did not come yesterday.
phrases.notes: So משיח cannot come today, שבת or יום טוב.

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁאנֵי הָתָם, דְּאָמַר קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof in Step 2 by giving another reason for the ברייתא's ruling.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from this ברייתא. It does not decide the question of תחומין in the air.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא's leniency on שבת can be explained by the rule that אליהו comes a day before משיח, without assuming יש תחומין.

steps.title: Then weekdays should be allowed too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the אליהו reason. If it worked, every weekday would also be permitted, since אליהו did not come the day before.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, on weekdays too, every single day should be permitted, since אליהו did not come yesterday!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the new reason from Step 3. It shows that the reason proves too much.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On any ordinary weekday we can also say 'אליהו did not come yesterday.' By Step 3's logic, wine should be allowed every day. But the ברייתא clearly forbids it on weekdays (Step 1), so the אליהו reason cannot be the whole story.

keyTerms.meaning: If so (introduces a challenge from the previous logic)

phrases.aramaic: אִי הָכִי, בְּחוֹל כֹּל יוֹמָא וְיוֹמָא נָמֵי לִישְׁתְּרֵי,
phrases.english: If so, on weekdays too, each and every day should be permitted,
phrases.notes: Applies Step 3's logic to weekdays.

phrases.english: since Elijah did not come yesterday?
phrases.notes: This contradicts the ברייתא's ruling in Step 1.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, בְּחוֹל כֹּל יוֹמָא וְיוֹמָא נָמֵי לִישְׁתְּרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the דחיה of Step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reason in Step 3 (אליהו did not come yesterday).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The reason would also permit wine on every weekday. That contradicts the ברייתא's ban on weekdays.

steps.title: Weekdays are forbidden because אליהו may have come quietly to the court
steps.stepSummary: Still inside its challenge, the גמרא states the accepted reason weekdays are forbidden: אליהו may have come only to the בית דין הגדול, without the public knowing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, we say: he may have come to the בית דין הגדול.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the weekday ban. This sets up its final move in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אליהו might have arrived yesterday but announced himself only to the High Court, so ordinary people do not know yet. That is why we cannot rely on 'he did not come yesterday' on weekdays.

keyTerms.meaning: The Great Court (the סנהדרין in ירושלים)

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אָמְרִינַן: לְבֵית דִּין הַגָּדוֹל אֲתָא.
phrases.english: Rather, we say: he came to the Great Court.
phrases.notes: אליהו might have come privately, so the news has not reached us.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמְרִינַן: לְבֵית דִּין הַגָּדוֹל אֲתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the weekday ban as part of the challenge to Step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explaining the reason behind the ruling
steps.terutzHavaAmina: That 'אליהו did not come yesterday' would permit wine on every day.
steps.terutzMaskana: Weekdays are forbidden because אליהו might have come quietly to the בית דין הגדול.

steps.title: The same worry should apply to שבת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns the explanation back on Step 3. On שבת too, we should worry that אליהו came on Friday to the בית דין הגדול.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too, let us say: he came (yesterday, on ערב שבת) to the בית דין הגדול!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its attack on the אליהו reason. The same worry should apply on שבת, so the אליהו reason cannot explain why wine is allowed then.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If we worry on weekdays that אליהו came quietly to the court yesterday, we must worry the same way about Friday. Then the אליהו verse does not explain the leniency on שבת. That points back to the original idea from Step 2, that יש תחומין.
steps.whatToRemember: At this point the reason 'אליהו did not come yesterday' seems to fail, because he might have come quietly to the בית דין הגדול on ערב שבת. The next step answers this challenge.

phrases.english: Here too, let us say:
phrases.notes: Applies the weekday worry to שבת and יום טוב.

phrases.english: he came to the Great Court?
phrases.notes: He could have come on ערב שבת or ערב יום טוב, so the אליהו reason doesn't work.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכָא נָמֵי לֵימָא: לְבֵית דִּין הַגָּדוֹל אֲתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses Step 5's explanation to reject the דחיה of Step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reason in Step 3 for why wine is allowed on שבת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If we worry that אליהו came quietly to the court before a weekday, we must also worry he came on Friday, so the אליהו reason cannot explain the leniency on שבת.

steps.title: אליהו Will Not Come on ערב שבת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the challenge from Step 6. It is promised that אליהו will not come on ערב שבת or ערב יום טוב, because it would disturb people's preparations.
steps.simpleTranslation: It has already been promised to the Jewish people that אליהו will not come on the eve of שבת or on the eve of a יום טוב, because of the bother it would cause.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the worry from Step 6, which asked: maybe אליהו came on Friday to the בית דין הגדול. It answers that אליהו never comes on a Friday or on the day before a יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 6 argued that שבת should be forbidden, just like a weekday, because אליהו might have come quietly on Friday. This answer removes that possibility completely: there is a promise that he will not come on a Friday. So on שבת we can be sure that אליהו did not come the day before, and the נזיר may drink wine.

keyTerms.meaning: the days before a יום טוב
bother, effort; here, the busy work of getting ready for שבת

phrases.english: It has already been promised to the Jewish people
that Elijah will not come
neither on the eves of Shabbat
nor on the eves of Festivals,
because of the bother.
phrases.notes: People would go out to greet him and would not finish preparing for שבת.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּבָר מוּבְטָח לָהֶן לְיִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 6 by ruling out a Friday arrival of אליהו.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Brings a new fact (a promise) that removes the feared possibility.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: אליהו might have come on Friday to the בית דין הגדול, so שבת should be forbidden just like a weekday.
steps.terutzMaskana: אליהו never comes on ערב שבת or ערב יום טוב, so on שבת and יום טוב we know he did not come the day before.

steps.title: Should Wine Also Be Allowed on Friday?
steps.stepSummary: If אליהו cannot come on Friday, then משיח cannot come on Saturday. Perhaps this also means משיח cannot come on Friday, and so Friday should be permitted too.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think: since אליהו does not come on Friday, משיח also does not come on Friday. If so, the נזיר should be allowed to drink wine on Friday as well!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes the new rule one step further. It suggests that the promise about Friday might also cover משיח himself, so wine should be allowed on Friday.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason for the promise is the bother of the preparations. That same reason seems to apply to משיח's arrival. If so, the ברייתא should have permitted Friday too, but it did not.

keyTerms.meaning: it might enter your mind; you might think

phrases.english: It might enter your mind
that since Elijah does not come,
the Messiah also does not come,
so on Shabbat eve he should be permitted!

steps.triggerLanguage: קָא סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ מִדְּאֵלִיָּהוּ לָא אֲתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the Friday promise from Step 7 and asks whether it also covers משיח himself.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's ruling that the נזיר is forbidden to drink wine on Friday (a weekday).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The reason that keeps אליהו away on Friday (the bother) should keep משיח away too, so Friday should be permitted.

steps.title: משיח Can Still Come on Friday
steps.stepSummary: Only אליהו is kept away on Friday. משיח himself can come, because once he arrives the nations will serve the Jewish people and help with the preparations.
steps.simpleTranslation: אליהו does not come on Friday, but משיח can come. Once משיח comes, everyone will be servants to the Jewish people.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 8. It explains why משיח can come on Friday even though אליהו cannot.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The promise is based on the bother of preparing for שבת. When משיח comes, the nations will do the work for the Jewish people, so there is no bother. Therefore משיח might come on Friday, and the נזיר must still avoid wine then.

phrases.english: Elijah does not come, but the Messiah does come.
For once the Messiah comes —
all are servants to the Jewish people.
phrases.notes: The nations will help prepare for שבת, so there is no bother.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵלִיָּהוּ לָא אָתֵי, מָשִׁיחַ אָתֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 8 by showing that the reason for the promise (bother) does not apply to משיח.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction: the reason applies to אליהו but not to משיח.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since אליהו does not come on Friday, משיח does not come either, so Friday should be permitted.
steps.terutzMaskana: משיח can come on Friday, because the nations will do the preparation work. So Friday stays forbidden.

steps.title: Should Wine Be Allowed on Sunday?
steps.stepSummary: If אליהו cannot come on שבת, then משיח cannot come on Sunday. So the נזיר should be allowed wine on Sunday too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then let him be permitted to drink wine on Sunday!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new challenge. If אליהו cannot travel on שבת, then משיח cannot arrive on Sunday, so Sunday should be permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If תחומין apply above ten טפחים, אליהו cannot come on שבת. That means משיח, who comes the day after אליהו, cannot come on Sunday. Yet the ברייתא does not permit Sunday, and this sets up the next move.

keyTerms.meaning: Sunday, the first day of the week

phrases.english: On Sunday he should be permitted?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּחַד בְּשַׁבָּא לִישְׁתְּרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same pattern as before (משיח comes the day after אליהו) and applies it to Sunday.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's ruling that the נזיר is forbidden to drink wine on Sunday.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If אליהו cannot come on שבת (because of תחומין), משיח cannot come on Sunday, so Sunday should be permitted.

steps.title: A Proof That There Are No תחומין Above Ten טפחים
steps.stepSummary: Since the ברייתא does not permit Sunday, the גמרא tries to prove that תחומין do not apply above ten טפחים. If they did apply, Sunday would be permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us conclude from this that there are no תחומין above ten טפחים. For if there were תחומין, Sunday should be permitted, since אליהו could not have come on שבת!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the Sunday question into a proof. The ברייתא forbids Sunday, so it must hold that אליהו can travel on שבת, meaning there are no תחומין above ten טפחים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אליהו travels through the air, above ten טפחים. If תחומין applied there, he could not come on שבת, and Sunday would be safe. Since the ברייתא still forbids Sunday, it seems to hold that תחומין do not apply above ten.

keyTerms.meaning: let us resolve (the question) from it
there are no שבת travel limits (above ten טפחים)
there are שבת travel limits (above ten טפחים)

steps.confusionAlert: Notice the flip: in Step 2 the ברייתא seemed to prove that תחומין DO apply above ten (because of שבת). Now the same ברייתא seems to prove that they do NOT apply (because of Sunday). The two halves of the ברייתא pull in opposite directions.

phrases.english: Let us resolve from it that there are no Shabbat limits,
for if there are Shabbat limits —
on Sunday he should be permitted,
since Elijah did not come on Shabbat?!

steps.triggerLanguage: לִפְשׁוֹט מִינַּהּ דְּאֵין תְּחוּמִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the Sunday question of Step 10 into a proof about the open question of תחומין above ten טפחים.
steps.raayaObject: That תחומין do not apply above ten טפחים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא forbids wine on Sunday, which only makes sense if אליהו could have come on שבת.

steps.title: The תנא Was Unsure, So He Ruled Strictly
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. This תנא was unsure whether תחומין apply above ten טפחים, so he ruled strictly and forbade Sunday. Permitting שבת does not depend on תחומין at all; it rests on the promise that אליהו does not come on ערב שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: This תנא was in doubt whether there are תחומין or there are no תחומין, and he ruled strictly.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the proof from Step 11. The ברייתא does not take a side on תחומין; the תנא was simply unsure and acted strictly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because of the doubt, the תנא could not rely on 'אליהו cannot come on שבת', so he kept Sunday forbidden. Permitting שבת does not depend on תחומין at all, because of the promise in Step 7. So the ברייתא proves nothing either way, and the question of תחומין above ten טפחים stays open.

keyTerms.meaning: a sage of the משנה period; here, the author of the ברייתא

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא of the נזיר for משיח proves nothing about תחומין above ten טפחים. שבת and יום טוב are permitted because of the promise that אליהו does not come on their eves. Sunday is forbidden because the תנא was unsure about תחומין and ruled strictly.
steps.whyThisMatters: It closes this whole attempt to settle the question of תחומין above ten טפחים from this ברייתא. The question remains unresolved.

phrases.english: This tanna was in doubt
whether there are Shabbat limits
or there are no Shabbat limits,
and so he ruled strictly.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַאי תַּנָּא סַפּוֹקֵי מְסַפְּקָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of Step 11 by saying the תנא's ruling comes from doubt, not from a firm position.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof that אין תחומין above ten טפחים. Together with Step 7, it also shows the ברייתא does not prove יש תחומין.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the תנא had a firm view on תחומין. In fact he was unsure and simply ruled strictly.

steps.title: When did the person make his vow?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks on which day the נזיר of the ברייתא made his vow.
steps.simpleTranslation: When did he get up and make the vow?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question about the ברייתא's case: on what day did this person vow to be a נזיר? This question sets up the next two moves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said this נזיר may drink wine on שבת and יום טוב, because משיח will not come on those days. The גמרא wants to know when the vow was made, because the day of the vow determines whether a 'wine-free' day can even happen.

keyTerms.meaning: a person who vows to avoid wine and other items

phrases.english: When did he arise and make the vow?
phrases.notes: Refers to the person who vowed to be a נזיר 'on the day בן דוד comes'.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּקָאֵי אֵימַת דְּקָא נָדַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After settling the שבת and Sunday questions, the גמרא now asks about the timing of the vow itself.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: On which day of the week the vow was made.

steps.title: A weekday vow cannot work
steps.stepSummary: If he vowed on a weekday, his נזירות already began, and שבת cannot cancel it.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say he vowed on a weekday, then his נזירות already took effect. How can שבת come and cancel it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the first possibility: that he vowed on a weekday. It shows this cannot fit the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On a weekday משיח might come that very day, so the נזירות takes effect right away. Once a person is a נזיר, his נזירות continues without a break. So a later שבת cannot suddenly allow him wine.

keyTerms.meaning: the status of being a נזיר

steps.confusionAlert: The problem is not that שבת is weaker than the vow. The point is that נזירות, once it has started, does not switch on and off from day to day.

phrases.english: If you say he arose and vowed on a weekday —
since the נזירות has already taken effect on him,
how can שבת come and cancel it?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵּימָא דְּקָאֵי בְּחוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests and rejects the first possible answer to the question in step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that the vow was made on a weekday.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A vow made on a weekday puts the נזירות into effect at once. Since נזירות does not stop once it has begun, a later שבת cannot permit wine.

steps.title: He vowed on שבת or יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: The vow was made on שבת or יום טוב. Only that day is permitted; afterward he is forbidden for good.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he arose and vowed on שבת, or on יום טוב. That one day is permitted to him. From then on, he is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question: the ברייתא is speaking about someone who vowed on שבת or יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On the day of the vow משיח cannot come, so the נזירות has not started yet, and he may drink wine. Once a weekday arrives, the נזירות takes effect. From that point it continues, even on later שבתות and ימים טובים.
steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא's permission to drink wine on שבת and יום טוב covers only the first day, when he vowed on that day. Once his נזירות begins on a weekday, it never pauses again.

phrases.english: Rather, he arose on שבת and vowed,
or on יום טוב and vowed,
and it is only that day that is permitted to him,
from then on — he is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא דְּקָאֵי בְּשַׁבְּתָא וְקָא נָדַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the correct answer after step 14 rejected the weekday option.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He vowed on שבת or יום טוב. Only that day is permitted, and afterward the נזירות is permanent.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The ברייתא's permission applies only to the day of the vow, when that day is שבת or יום טוב.

steps.title: Back to the משנה: the boat that reached port late
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about the time the boat did not enter the port before nightfall.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'One time they did not enter the port until nightfall,' and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא leaves the topic of the נזיר and returns to the משנה. It quotes the story of רבן גמליאל's boat to begin explaining it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, the boat arrived after nightfall on ערב שבת. רבן גמליאל ruled that the passengers could get off, because the boat had already entered the city's תחום before שבת began. Quoting the משנה here sets up the explanation that follows.

phrases.aramaic: פַּעַם אַחַת לֹא נִכְנְסוּ לַנָּמָל וְכוּ׳.
phrases.english: One time they did not enter the port, etc.

steps.triggerLanguage: פַּעַם אַחַת לֹא נִכְנְסוּ לַנָּמָל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new section: the גמרא returns to the משנה after the side-discussion about the נזיר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Quotes the משנה: the boat entered the port after nightfall, and רבן גמליאל permitted the passengers to get off.

steps.title: רבן גמליאל's measuring tube
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that רבן גמליאל had a tube for seeing 2,000 אמות, on land and at sea.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא taught: רבן גמליאל had a tube that he would look through. With it he could see 2,000 אמות on land, and the matching 2,000 at sea.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that explains how רבן גמליאל knew the boat was already inside the תחום before שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Distances are hard to judge at sea. The tube let רבן גמליאל measure 2,000 אמות, which is the size of a תחום שבת, both on land and on water. That is how he could rule that the boat had entered the city's limit in time.

keyTerms.meaning: 2,000 cubits, the size of a תחום שבת

steps.whyThisMatters: This explains the basis for רבן גמליאל's ruling in the משנה. He did not guess; he measured the תחום with a tool.

phrases.aramaic: תָּנָא: שְׁפוֹפֶרֶת הָיְתָה לוֹ לְרַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
phrases.english: It was taught: Rabban Gamliel had a tube
through which he would look and see
two thousand cubits on land,
and corresponding to it, two thousand at sea.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא: שְׁפוֹפֶרֶת הָיְתָה לוֹ לְרַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how רבן גמליאל in the משנה knew where the boat was.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבן גמליאל used a tube to measure 2,000 אמות on land and at sea.

steps.title: Using a tube to measure a valley's depth
steps.stepSummary: Anyone who wants to know a valley's depth can look through a tube, like רבן גמליאל's, and figure it out.
steps.simpleTranslation: Someone who wants to know how deep a valley is can bring a tube, look through it, and he will know how deep the valley is.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues from רבן גמליאל's tube. It teaches that anyone can use a tube like that to measure how deep a valley is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 17 said רבן גמליאל's tube could measure 2,000 אמות, the length of a תחום שבת. Here the same tool is applied to another measurement: depth. The point is that the tube is a real measuring tool that anyone can use, not something special to רבן גמליאל.

keyTerms.meaning: A tube or pipe used for sighting distances

phrases.aramaic: הָרוֹצֶה לֵידַע כַּמָּה עוֹמְקוֹ שֶׁל גֵּיא,
phrases.english: One who wishes to know how deep a valley is,
brings a tube and looks through it,
and he will know how deep the valley is.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָרוֹצֶה לֵידַע כַּמָּה עוֹמְקוֹ שֶׁל גֵּיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the use of רבן גמליאל's tube from measuring distance to measuring depth.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A sighting tube can be used to measure the depth of a valley.

steps.title: Using shadows to measure a palm tree's height
steps.stepSummary: A person can find a palm tree's height by comparing his own height and shadow with the palm tree's shadow.
steps.simpleTranslation: Someone who wants to know how tall a palm tree is measures his own height and his own shadow, and then the tree's shadow. From these he will know how tall the palm tree is.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second measuring trick. You can find a tree's height without climbing it by using shadows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Your height compared to your shadow is the same ratio as the tree's height compared to its shadow. For example, if your shadow equals your height, then the tree's shadow equals the tree's height. You measure three things and work out the fourth.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָרוֹצֶה לֵידַע כַּמָּה גּוֹבְהוֹ שֶׁל דֶּקֶל —
phrases.english: And one who wishes to know how tall a palm tree is
measures his own height and his own shadow,
and the shadow of its height,
phrases.notes: Meaning the length of the palm tree's shadow.

phrases.english: and he will know how tall the palm tree is.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָרוֹצֶה לֵידַע כַּמָּה גּוֹבְהוֹ שֶׁל דֶּקֶל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second measurement technique, using shadows and proportion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A tree's height can be calculated from the ratio of a person's height to his shadow.

steps.title: Angling a grave so animals won't rest in its shade
steps.stepSummary: To keep wild animals from resting in a grave's shade, check the direction of a reed's shadow at the fourth hour. Then slant the gravestone so it casts no shade.
steps.simpleTranslation: Someone who does not want a wild animal to rest in the shade of a grave sticks a reed in the ground at the fourth hour of the day. He sees which way its shadow leans, then slants the grave marker up and down accordingly.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a third practical shadow technique. This one protects the honor of a grave by making sure it gives no shade where animals would lie down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By the fourth hour the sun is hot, and animals look for shade. The reed shows exactly which way shadows fall at that time. The gravestone is then tilted to match, so it casts no useful shade, and animals will not gather there.

phrases.aramaic: הָרוֹצֶה שֶׁלֹּא תִּשְׁרֶה חַיָּה רָעָה בְּצֵל קֶבֶר —
phrases.english: One who wishes that a wild animal not rest in the shade of a grave
sticks a reed in the ground at the fourth hour of the day,
and sees in which direction its shadow leans,
and slants the grave marker upward and slants it downward.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָרוֹצֶה שֶׁלֹּא תִּשְׁרֶה חַיָּה רָעָה בְּצֵל קֶבֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the series of shadow-based practical techniques.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Tilt the grave marker in line with the fourth-hour shadow so that it casts no shade for animals.
steps.whatToRemember: These three techniques (tube, shadow ratio, angled gravestone) close out the side discussion that grew from רבן גמליאל's tube.

steps.title: נחמיה walks past the Shabbat limit while learning
steps.stepSummary: נחמיה, son of רב חנילאי, was so absorbed in learning that he walked outside the תחום שבת without noticing.
steps.simpleTranslation: נחמיה, son of רב חנילאי, was carried away by his learning, and he went out beyond the תחום.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the topic of the תחום and starts a story. This sets up a real case: a person who is now stuck outside his תחום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case connects to the משנה's discussion of someone who ends up outside the תחום. נחמיה left by accident, while focused on Torah. This sets up the question of what can be done for such a person.

keyTerms.meaning: A Torah teaching or topic of study

phrases.english: Nechemya, son of Rav Chanilai,
was drawn along by his learning,
and went out beyond the Shabbat limit.

steps.triggerLanguage: נְחֶמְיָה בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב חֲנִילַאי מְשַׁכְתֵּיהּ שְׁמַעְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the measuring techniques behind and opens a story about someone who left the תחום.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets up the case of a person who accidentally ended up outside the תחום.

steps.title: רב חסדא tells רב נחמן that his student is stuck
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא tells רב נחמן that his student נחמיה is in distress. He is implicitly asking what can be done to help.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said to רב נחמן: Your student נחמיה is in distress.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא raises the problem with רב נחמן. This line sets up the next move, where a solution for נחמיה will be offered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On the surface this is a statement, but its function is a request for a solution: how can נחמיה get back inside? Being in distress here means he cannot return within the תחום on his own.

keyTerms.meaning: In distress, in a troubled state

steps.confusionAlert: This is not just sympathy. Classified by its function, רב חסדא's sentence is a question asking for a halachic solution.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב חִסְדָּא לְרַב נַחְמָן:
phrases.english: Rav Chisda said to Rav Nachman:
Your student Nechemya is in distress.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב חִסְדָּא לְרַב נַחְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns נחמיה's situation into a problem that needs a solution.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How can נחמיה, who is stuck outside the תחום, be helped to return?

steps.title: רב נחמן: Make a human wall so he can come back in
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן answers רב חסדא: form a partition out of people around נחמיה so that he can walk back into the תחום שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: He (רב נחמן) said to him: Make a partition of people for him, and let him come back in.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן answers רב חסדא's worry about נחמיה. People should stand in a row and form a 'wall', so נחמיה can walk inside it back into the permitted area.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, someone who goes past the תחום שבת is very limited in where he may walk. A line of people can count as a מחיצה, making one enclosed space that links נחמיה to the תחום. Once he is 'inside' that enclosure, he may walk through it and return.

keyTerms.meaning: A 'human partition', meaning a wall made of people standing in a row
And let him enter (come back in)

steps.confusionAlert: The people forming the wall are not breaking שבת themselves. They are people who are allowed to be standing there, for example because they made an עירוב. The question of exactly who these people are is what the גמרא is about to explore.
steps.whyThisMatters: This practical answer becomes the starting point for the whole next discussion. The גמרא now asks what רב חסדא was unsure about that made this answer necessary.

phrases.english: He said to him: Make for him a partition
phrases.notes: רב נחמן answering רב חסדא

phrases.english: of people, and let him enter.
phrases.notes: People line up to form walls, and נחמיה walks back through them

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ: עֲשֵׂה לוֹ מְחִיצָה שֶׁל בְּנֵי אָדָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב חסדא's implied request (Step 22) for a way to help נחמיה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How can נחמיה, who is stuck outside the תחום, get back in?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Make a human partition so he can walk inside it back into the תחום.

steps.title: What exactly was רב חסדא unsure about?
steps.stepSummary: The scene is set in the study hall: רב נחמן בר יצחק, sitting behind רבא, asks him what רב חסדא's actual question was.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק sat behind רבא, and רבא sat in front of רב נחמן. רב נחמן בר יצחק said to רבא: What was רב חסדא unsure about?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא describes the seating in רב נחמן's study hall and then reports a question. רב נחמן בר יצחק asks רבא: what was the real doubt behind רב חסדא's request? This sets up the analysis that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא is a great scholar, so he surely knew the basic idea of a human partition. So what specific point was he unsure about, which made him go ask רב נחמן? The גמרא will now try out possible answers one by one.

keyTerms.meaning: What was he unsure about? (What was his question?)

steps.confusionAlert: There are two different people named רב נחמן here. 'רב נחמן' is the teacher whom רב חסדא asked. 'רב נחמן בר יצחק' is a student sitting behind רבא, and he is the one asking the question.

phrases.aramaic: יָתֵיב רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק אֲחוֹרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא,
phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak sat behind Rava,
phrases.notes: Describes the seating rows in the study hall

phrases.english: and Rava sat in front of Rav Nachman.
phrases.notes: רבא was in the front row before the teacher

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק לְרָבָא:
phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said to Rava:

phrases.aramaic: מַאי קָא מִבַּעְיָא לֵיהּ לְרַב חִסְדָּא?
phrases.english: What was Rav Chisda's question?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי קָא מִבַּעְיָא לֵיהּ לְרַב חִסְדָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Steps back from רב נחמן's answer to ask what the underlying question was.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact legal doubt that led רב חסדא to ask רב נחמן about נחמיה.

steps.title: First suggestion: Was the question whether the law follows רבן גמליאל?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא's first try: if the area was full of people who could form a wall, maybe רב חסדא was asking whether the הלכה follows רבן גמליאל, who lets a person walk through a whole enclosed area. This idea continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say we are dealing with a case where the area was filled with people, then he was asking: Is the הלכה like רבן גמליאל, ...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a first possible answer to what רב חסדא was asking. It is only a suggestion, and the sentence continues on the next amud, where the idea will be tested.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Suppose there really were enough people available to form a wall. Then the only doubt left is a legal one. רבן גמליאל holds that a person inside an enclosure may walk through all of it, even though he did not set up his place there before שבת. If the הלכה follows him, a human enclosure would let נחמיה walk back in. The word אילימא ('if you say') is a signal that this suggestion will probably be challenged.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (introduces a suggestion that is often later rejected)
That it was filled with men (enough people were present)

steps.confusionAlert: This step is not finished. The sentence continues on the next amud, which presents the other side of the question and then tests it. Do not treat this as the גמרא's final conclusion.

phrases.english: If you say we are dealing with a case where it was filled with people,
phrases.notes: Enough people were present who could legally stand there and form a wall

phrases.english: and his question was:
Is the halacha like Rabban Gamliel,
phrases.notes: רבן גמליאל allows walking through an entire enclosure. The sentence continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵּימָא בִּדְמָלוּ גַּבְרֵי עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers the first possible answer to רב נחמן בר יצחק's question in Step 24.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A tentative suggestion: if enough people were available, the doubt was whether the הלכה follows רבן גמליאל about walking through an enclosure. The suggestion continues and will be tested.
